answers.answer: The summary says a clearing is ruled by the player with the most combined warriors and buildings, and that ties mean no one rules. It does not explain Eyrie-specific ties, tokens, or the Vagabond pawn, so those parts are unsupported.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases: ‘most combined warriors and buildings’; ‘Ties mean no one rules.’

answers.answer: A normal move is from a clearing to an adjacent connected clearing, and the mover must rule either the origin or destination. The summary does not say whether the same warriors may move repeatedly or whether rivers count as paths.
answers.evidence: Shared Rules for All Factions—Movement: ‘adjacent connected clearing’ and ‘rule ... the origin or destination.’

answers.answer: A defender may play a matching-suit Ambush card at the start of battle to deal 2 hits before dice. The attacker rolls two dice; the higher die gives attacker hits and the lower gives defender hits, with maximum hits limited by warriors present. Remove warriors before tokens/buildings, and the attacker scores 1 VP for each removed building or token. The summary does not describe foiling ambushes, early ending, extra hits, or clarify the warrior limit per side.
answers.evidence: Shared Rules—Battle and Special Rules: ‘Ambush cards ... at the start of battle to deal 2 hits’; ‘Remove warriors first, then tokens/buildings’; each removed building or token scores ‘1 VP for the attacker.’

answers.answer: Crafting uses cards matching the suits of clearings where the faction has crafting pieces. The summary gives examples of crafting pieces by faction, but does not state costs per crafted item, whether a piece can be used repeatedly, what happens when the needed item is absent from the supply, or how duplicate persistent effects work.
answers.evidence: Shared Rules—Crafting: ‘Spend cards matching the suits of clearings where you have crafting pieces.’

answers.answer: The summary says the first player to reach 30 VP wins immediately. A player may instead play a Dominance card to change their win condition to controlling 3 specific clearings at the start of their next Birdsong; other players may also adopt Dominance. It does not give activation VP thresholds, the winning clearing pattern for each suit, or replacement/discard rules for an activated card.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘play a Dominance card’ and ‘controlling 3 specific clearings at the start of their next Birdsong.’

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary does not say what happens to a dominance card spent for its suit or how another player can take it, including a bird dominance card.
answers.evidence: No section describes dominance cards being spent for suit or taken by another player.

answers.answer: The general setup says to shuffle the shared deck, deal 3 cards to each player, and place items on ruin spaces and in the supply. It does not specify the standard two-player deck change, resulting hand size, or faction setup order.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Shuffle the shared deck and deal 3 cards to each player’; ‘Place item tokens on the map's ruin spaces and in the supply.’

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary does not explain what the Keep forbids or permits, Field Hospitals, or rebuilding the Keep.
answers.evidence: No section describes the Keep or Field Hospitals.

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight lists Battle, March, Recruit, Build, and Overwork as available actions, with 3 actions plus 1 bonus action per bird card. March is identified as moving, Recruit places warriors at recruiters, and Overwork spends a card to produce extra wood. The summary does not state the precise Daylight order, number of moves per March, or a Recruit limit.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat—Daylight: ‘Battle, March (move), Recruit (place warriors at recruiters), Build ... Overwork (spend a card to produce extra wood)’ and ‘3 actions + 1 bonus action per bird card.’

answers.answer: The summary says Marquise builds buildings using wood and scores VP for building workshops, sawmills, and recruiters, with escalating VP for each new building of a type. It does not explain the rule requirement, wood network, or how to select a track space when building.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat: ‘Build (place buildings using wood)’; scores VP by building the three building types, with ‘escalating VP.’

answers.answer: The summary says the Eyrie adds 1–2 cards to the Decree during Birdsong. It does not state a recovery placement requirement when there are no roosts.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties—Birdsong: ‘Add 1-2 cards to the Decree.’

answers.answer: The Eyrie resolves the Decree in the order Recruit, Move, Battle, Build roosts; each card forces actions in matching-suit clearings. The summary does not explain within-column order or the restrictions on Build.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties—Daylight: ‘Resolve the Decree in order: Recruit, Move, Battle, Build roosts’; ‘Each card ... forces actions in matching-suit clearings.’

answers.answer: The summary says failure to fulfill any Decree action causes Turmoil: lose VP equal to the number of bird cards in the Decree, remove all warriors and buildings except roosts, choose a new leader, and reset the Decree. It does not describe Viziers or what happens to the rest of the turn.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Turmoil: ‘lose VP equal to the number of bird cards in the Decree,’ remove pieces ‘except roosts,’ ‘choose a new leader,’ and ‘reset the Decree.’

answers.answer: The summary says another player must give the Alliance a card when entering or battling in a sympathetic clearing. It does not specify the precise trigger timing, which card is paid, or what happens if the player has no matching card or the supporter stack is full.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance: ‘Other players must give the Alliance a card when entering or battling in sympathetic clearings.’

answers.answer: During Alliance Birdsong, the summary describes Revolt as spending supporters to place a base and warriors and remove all enemy pieces from a clearing; Spread Sympathy spends supporters to place sympathy tokens. It does not give their precise timing/order, eligible clearings, supporter costs, or martial law rules.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance—Birdsong: ‘Revolt (spend supporters to place a base and warriors, removing all enemy pieces from a clearing) or Spread Sympathy (spend supporters to place sympathy tokens).’

answers.answer: The summary says Train spends cards from the supporters stack to add officers, Mobilize adds cards to that stack, and Evening Organize draws cards. It does not say how losing a base affects supporters or officers.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance—Daylight: ‘Mobilize (add cards to supporters stack), Train (spend cards from supporters to add officers)’; Evening: ‘organize (draw cards).’

answers.answer: The Vagabond refreshes exhausted items and may Slip during Birdsong, moving without ruling. A normal move follows the shared adjacent-connected-clearing rule and requires ruling the origin or destination. In Evening, the Vagabond may rest in a forest to repair all items or draw cards. The summary does not describe hostile destinations or the precise Evening draw rule.
answers.evidence: Vagabond: ‘Refresh exhausted items, slip (move without ruling)’; ‘Rest in forest (repair all items) or draw cards.’ Shared Movement describes the normal move rule.

answers.answer: Explore requires exhausting a torch; Quest requires discarding 2 matching-suit cards for VP. Repair is listed as a Daylight special action, but the summary gives no repair costs or procedure, item-side details, or precise quest/explore reward amounts.
answers.evidence: Vagabond—Daylight: ‘Explore ruins (exhaust torch)’ and ‘Quest (discard 2 matching-suit cards for VP)’; Repair is listed among the actions.

answers.answer: The summary says removing 3 of a faction's warriors makes it Hostile, and that aiding factions improves relations. It does not say when Infamy is scored, whether Aid can undo Hostility, or what Strike targets.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Hostile/Allied Relations: ‘Removing 3 of a faction's warriors makes them Hostile. Aiding factions improves relations.’

answers.answer: The summary says the Vagabond may form a coalition with the lowest-scoring player and shares that player's win condition. It does not give eligibility, timing, a VP requirement, detailed partner selection, or the effect of a Hostile relationship with the partner.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘The Vagabond may form a coalition with the lowest-scoring player, sharing that player's win condition.’
